statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-111497 (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35): a buffer overflow in the Google Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 lets a crafted Brotli stream corrupt decoder state, disclose memory, crash the program or possibly run code. Upstream fixed it in 1.2.1, 1.1.1 and 1.0.10 (https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.1, fix commit https://github.com/google/brotli/commit/b418fa81c48262a86a95332b0bc6d62c30aa78b6 in v1.2.1, which also adds the BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error code). Alpine fixed it in brotli 1.2.1-r0 (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.23/main.json). The DHI Alpine 3.23 repository publishes brotli 1.2.0-r0 and 1.2.1-r0, built from Alpine's brotli package source for upstream 1.2.0 and 1.2.1. We checked the brotli-libs, brotli-static, py3-brotli and brotli packages of both builds for x86_64 and aarch64 against the index checksum: 1.2.0-r0 ships libbrotlidec.so.1.2.0, whose error-name strings lack _ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH, and 1.2.1-r0 ships libbrotlidec.so.1.2.1, which contains it. The py3-brotli package, whose extension module compiles in its own copy of the decoder, shows the same split, and so does libbrotlidec.a in brotli-static, whose decode object holds link-time-optimization data in which the error name appears only in the 1.2.1-r0 build. The brotli program links libbrotlidec.so.1 dynamically. The range ends at 1.2.1-r0.

statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-111497 (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35) is an out-of-bounds write in the Google Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0: a crafted Brotli stream can corrupt decoder state, disclose memory or run code. Microsoft fixed the copy of the Brotli decoder that .NET bundles in .NET 10.0.14 (https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/494, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/10.0/10.0.14/10.0.14.md, https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.1). DHI dotnet10-runtime for Alpine 3.24 builds .NET 10 for Linux from Microsoft's source release with Alpine's build recipe, which removes the bundled Brotli sources and links Alpine's brotli library instead (UseSystemLibs includes brotli in https://github.com/alpinelinux/aports/blob/3e79705029656d3e638db79420fdbd21bf0e5212/community/dotnet10-runtime/APKBUILD). Scanned all 154 packages of the seven published builds (10.0.8-r0, 10.0.9-r0, 10.0.10-r0, 10.0.12-r0, 10.0.13-r0, 10.0.14-r0 and 10.0.15-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the files inside their nupkg and tar.gz archives, and read every ELF file and static archive in them: every copy of libSystem.IO.Compression.Native.so, and every other ELF file that refers to Brotli (the singlefilehost app hosts), lists libbrotlidec.so.1 and libbrotlienc.so.1 as needed libraries, and in the copies checked symbol by symbol (10.0.13-r0 x86_64, and every ELF file in the x86_64 10.0.8-r0 dotnet10-runtime-bootstrap package) every Brotli function is an undefined import. In that 10.0.8-r0 package, checked member by member, the static libSystem.IO.Compression.Native.a archives of the NativeAOT runtime packs hold two object files (pal_zlib.c.o and entrypoints.c.o), and none of its static archives defines a Brotli function. Every dotnet10-runtime package declares a dependency on libbrotlidec.so.1. No build of this owner contains its own copy of the Brotli decoder: it runs the decoder from Alpine's brotli package, which carries the fix from 1.2.1-r0 (https://secdb.alpinelinux.org/v3.24/main.json) and is assessed as its own owner.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-111497 is a buffer overflow in the decoder of Google's C Brotli library (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35). github.com/andybalholm/brotli, a Go port of Brotli, has the same bug before v1.2.7: its maintainer's advisory, GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv, says an invalid block-switch command can make the decoder read past the end of its input, which in Go is a panic or an infinite loop (a denial of service) rather than a buffer overflow, and the Go vulnerability entry GO-2026-6888 also describes unbounded Huffman-table allocations on crafted streams. v1.2.7 fixes it with a port of the upstream Brotli change that detects invalid streams earlier (https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6888, https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/security/advisories/GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv, https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/commit/33c2a9884269798192b5ecf171288f98939dbe42, https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.7). We checked every published jaeger-dev package for Alpine 3.24 in the DHI Alpine repository, 21 builds from 2.19.0-r1 to 2.23.0-r4, on x86_64 and aarch64 (42 packages), each against its index checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/jaeger, a Go program. Its symbol table contains the brotli decoder functions the advisory names, including github.com/andybalholm/brotli.(*Reader).Read, processCommandsInternal and decodeBlockTypeAndLength, in every build, so the vulnerable code is linked. Its Go build information shows github.com/andybalholm/brotli v1.2.0 in 2.19.0-r1 to 2.19.0-r4, v1.2.1 in 2.20.0-r0 to 2.20.0-r5, v1.2.2 in 2.21.0-r0 to 2.23.0-r0 and v1.2.7 from 2.23.0-r1 to 2.23.0-r4, the same on both architectures. The range ends at 2.23.0-r1, the first build with the fixed module.

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c). The CVE record lists Brotli from 1.0.3 before 1.0.10, 1.1.0 before 1.1.1, and 1.2.0 before 1.2.1 as affected. Node.js 22.x bundles Brotli 1.1.0 and decompresses Brotli data through node:zlib with it. Node.js lists 22.x as affected and fixed its bundled copy in 22.23.4, the 2026-10-21 security release, with commit 67d294739f, 'deps: brotli: cherry-pick 0ed4268a4401abcb44720963', and commit a18ec92752, which exposes the new BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error to node:zlib. Both carry this CVE id. Security release: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases#nodejs-brotli-decoder-out-of-bounds-write-permits-remote-code-execution-cve-2026-111497---high and commits: https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/67d294739f and https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/a18ec92752 are the sources. The bundled Brotli still reports version 1.1.0 after the cherry-pick, so the Brotli version alone does not show the fix. We read the node binary in every published DHI nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64, 13 builds from 22.22.0-r0 to the current 22.23.5-r0, each checked against its index checksum. 22.23.4-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v22.23.4 and contains the BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error name; 22.23.4-r1, 22.23.4-r2 and 22.23.5-r0 also contain it, and 22.22.0-r0 through 22.23.3-r0 report Node.js 22.22.0 through 22.23.3 and lack it. The decoder's own error string _ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH, which the cherry-picked decode.h change adds, is also present in 22.23.4-r0 and absent from 22.23.3-r0 (x86_64 binaries checked). No published build links a system Brotli library, so node:zlib always uses this bundled copy.

CVE-2026-111497 is an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c): an invalid block switch is reported as a need for more input instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder keeps appending input to an eight-byte internal buffer. The CVE record lists Brotli from 1.0.3 before 1.0.10, 1.1.0 before 1.1.1, and 1.2.0 before 1.2.1 as affected. Node.js 24.x bundles Brotli and decompresses Brotli data through node:zlib with it; the source tree bundles Brotli 1.1.0 at v24.13.0 and Brotli 1.2.0 at v24.22.0 and v24.22.1. Node.js lists 24.x as affected and fixed its bundled copy in 24.22.1, the 2026-10-21 security release, with commit 49dff6f57a, 'deps: brotli: cherry-pick 0ed4268a4401abcb44720963', and commit b5f41529df, which exposes the new BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error to node:zlib. Both carry this CVE id. Security release: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases#nodejs-brotli-decoder-out-of-bounds-write-permits-remote-code-execution-cve-2026-111497---high and commits: https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/49dff6f57a and https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/b5f41529df are the sources. Release notes: https://nodejs.org/en/blog/release/v24.22.1 list the fix. The cherry-pick does not change the bundled Brotli version, so the Brotli version alone does not show the fix. We read /usr/bin/node, the one program in the package, in every published DHI nodejs-24 package for Alpine 3.23, 18 builds from 24.13.0-r0 to the current 24.22.3-r0, on x86_64 and aarch64, each checked against its index checksum. 24.13.0-r0 through 24.22.0-r0 report Node.js 24.13.0 through 24.22.0 and lack the FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error name, while the 16 other BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_ names are found in the same scan; 24.22.1-r0 is the first build that reports Node.js v24.22.1 and contains it, and 24.22.1-r1, 24.22.2-r0 and 24.22.3-r0 contain it too. The decoder's own error string _ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH, which the cherry-picked decode.h change adds, is also present in 24.22.1-r0 and absent from 24.22.0-r0 (aarch64 binaries checked). In every one of these builds the node program's shared-library dependencies are libstdc++, libgcc_s and musl libc, with no system Brotli library, so node:zlib always uses the bundled copy. The range ends at 24.22.1-r0.

CVE-2026-111497 is a buffer overflow in the decoder of Google's C Brotli library: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35. github.com/andybalholm/brotli, a Go port of Brotli, has the same bug before v1.2.7: its maintainer's advisory GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv says an invalid block-switch command can make the decoder read past the end of its input, which in Go is a panic or an infinite loop (a denial of service) rather than a buffer overflow. The Go vulnerability entry GO-2026-6888, which lists CVE-2026-111497 and GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv as aliases, also describes unbounded Huffman-table allocations on crafted streams. v1.2.7 fixes it with a port of the upstream Brotli change that detects invalid streams earlier. Sources: https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/security/advisories/GHSA-c9gr-gmg4-2vqv, https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6888, https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/commit/33c2a9884269798192b5ecf171288f98939dbe42, https://github.com/andybalholm/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.7. We read the Go build information of /usr/bin/alloy in every published alloy-dev package for Debian 13 in the DHI Debian repository: 1.18.1-0 to 1.22.0-16, 43 versions on amd64 and 44 on arm64, where 1.21.2-0 is published for arm64 only, each matched to the repository's SHA-256 checksum. Each package holds one file, /usr/bin/alloy, a Go program. Every build before 1.21.3-0 is built with github.com/andybalholm/brotli 1.2.2 (1.18.1-0 to 1.19.2-7) or 1.2.4 (1.20.1-0 to 1.21.2-1), inside the affected range, and 1.21.3-0 and every later build with 1.2.7, the same on both architectures. The Go symbol table of /usr/bin/alloy in 1.21.2-1 (amd64), built with brotli 1.2.4, lists the advisory's decoder functions, among them github.com/andybalholm/brotli.(*Reader).Read, decodeBlockTypeAndLength, processCommandsInternal and the block-switch decoders, so the vulnerable code is linked. The range ends at 1.21.3-0, the first build with the fixed module.

The range ends at 1.21.3-0, the first build with the fixed module.

CVE-2026-111497 (GHSA-9v8h-qqgm-4m35): a buffer overflow in the Google Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 lets a crafted Brotli stream corrupt decoder state, disclose memory, crash the program or possibly run code. Upstream fixed it in 1.2.1, 1.1.1 and 1.0.10 (https://github.com/google/brotli/releases/tag/v1.2.1, fix commit https://github.com/google/brotli/commit/b418fa81c48262a86a95332b0bc6d62c30aa78b6 in v1.2.1, which also adds the BROTLI_DECODER_ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error code). Debian fixed it for trixie in brotli 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 (DSA-6582-1, Debian bug 1151690, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-111497). The DHI Debian repository publishes rebuilds of Debian 1.1.0-2+deb13u1, the lowest of which is the fixed version here, and an older rebuild of Debian 1.1.0-2 that predates the fix and sorts below it. We checked the libbrotli1, libbrotli-dev, python3-brotli and brotli packages of every published build for amd64 and arm64 against the index checksum: in the 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 rebuilds the shipped Debian changelog records the CVE-2026-111497 fix, and both libbrotlidec.so.1.1.0 and the python3-brotli extension module, which compiles in its own copy of the decoder rather than linking libbrotlidec, contain the _ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH error name the fix adds, as does libbrotlidec.a in libbrotli-dev; in the 1.1.0-2 rebuild none of them does. The brotli program links libbrotlidec.so.1 dynamically. Builds on both sides of the boundary ship upstream version 1.1.0 (libbrotlidec.so.1.1.0). The range ends at the first 1.1.0-2+deb13u1 rebuild.
